thread:
maria: heads-up — ran into a weird resolution bug with pnpm workspaces + our JS SDK when deploying to edge runtime (vercel edge). app builds locally but edge bundle can't find the SDK ESM entry.

maria: minimal error from Vercel: 
```
Error: Could not resolve '/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/sdk' from 'src/edge-handler.ts'
  at resolve (/vercel/build/....)
  at Object.resolveId (/snapshot/vite/node_modules/rollup/dist/shared/rollup.js:...)
```

jake: ugh. are you seeing a missing package.json or the exports map being ignored?

maria: looks like the bundler can't read package.json of the hoisted package. pnpm creates the nested .pnpm layout + symlinks and the edge builder's resolver is not following the symlink to the package root where exports are defined. My package.json for the consumer has normal dep on @redwood/sdk, sdk package has exports with import/require entries.

maria: consumer package.json snippet: 
```json
{
  "name": "@acme/web",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk": "^0.12.0"
  }
}
```

maria: sdk package.json exports: 
```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "exports": {
    ".": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs"},
    "./types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

tina: I've seen this before with pnpm + edge builders. Bundlers like esbuild/vite sometimes treat symlinked packages as "external" or fail to load package.json when they expect a real package dir. Two common workarounds: 1) configure pnpm to use node-linker=hoisted (makes layout closer to npm/yarn) or 2) make the bundler resolve to the actual dist file via alias.

sam: +1 on alias. For Vite you can do: 
```js
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@redwood/sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.mjs')
  }
}
```

sam: Another option: set "public-hoist-pattern" in .npmrc to hoist @redwood/sdk to top-level node_modules (so package.json is easy to find). That's less invasive than switching linkers.

jake: typings gotcha too: TS sometimes resolves types via the hoisted path differently. If your consumer uses project references or path mappings, you might need a typesVersions entry or explicitly reference the d.ts file in the alias.

maria: yeah the runtime error was first, but then tsc complained: "Cannot find type definition for '@redwood/sdk'" even though node resolution worked locally.

tina: For monorepos we add a tiny wrapper package in the workspace root that re-exports the built files and has a plain package.json with exports — this makes edge builders happier. Example: packages/sdk-wrapper/package.json -> { "name": "@acme/sdk-wrapper", "exports": {".": "./dist/index.mjs"} } and then depend on that from the app. Ugly but effective until bundlers improve.

maria: thanks. Immediate plan: try alias first (fast) and open a pnpm .npmrc change PR to test public-hoist-pattern. If that stabilizes, we'll add a short note to the devex docs and a tiny sample repo showing the Vite/Edge config.

jake: ping me on the PR, I can help test on our vercel account. Also might be good to add a troubleshooting subsection about "Edge bundlers + pnpm workspaces" in SDK onboarding.
